question: Can I reach you at 2am?
html:
Late-night calls

You can call us at 2am. Our data does not yet confirm whether a person or a voice agent answers at that hour, so overnight coverage is still unconfirmed.

What the data shows

  • Calls outside business hours are common. Off-hours calls made up 14.1% of HVAC inbound calls in June 2025 and 9.8% in October 2025. Most of them arrive between 5 and 9 pm local time (Punctual Pros demand model).
  • Trades lose 30-40% of off-hours calls (Voice AI research).
  • Across home services, 52% of callers reach a person. The figure is 65% for calls longer than 15 seconds (Voice AI research).
  • AI voice agents answer around the clock. One vendor reports they book 70% of calls, and 90% when crews have open slots. The typical human booking rate is 42%. These are vendor-reported and unaudited figures, so treat them as ranges (Voice AI research).

What we cannot confirm

  • Staffing: which hours a dispatcher or answering service covers today.
  • Answer rate at 2am: our actual answer rate overnight. Our call volume, missed-call rate and booking rate are not public. The model infers them from estimated revenue (Voice AI research).
  • Data that would settle it: hourly call logs from our ServiceTitan or CRM history. Answered, missed and booked counts by hour would answer both questions.

Why timing matters now

  • October is the busiest HVAC month nationally because heating systems start up (Punctual Pros demand model).
  • A lead reached within 5 minutes is 21 times more likely to qualify than one reached at 30 minutes (Voice AI research).

A 2am caller with no heat will dial the next number on Google. Recovering missed calls across all hours is modelled at about $1.37M a year (est.). Overnight calls are a measurable revenue line, not a courtesy.

Next actions

  1. Pull hourly answered, missed and booked counts for the last 12 months from ServiceTitan. This confirms overnight coverage and the real after-hours loss rate.
  2. Publish the actual overnight answering policy on the site once it is confirmed, so the reference answer can give a yes or no.
  3. Pilot an AI voice agent for overnight and storm overflow. Measure its booking rate against current human booking before rolling it out further.
  4. Re-run the recovered-revenue estimate with real call data, replacing the inferred call volume.
markdown:
# Late-night calls

You can call us at 2am. Our data does not yet confirm whether a person or a voice agent answers at that hour, so overnight coverage is still unconfirmed.

## What the data shows

- Calls outside business hours are common. Off-hours calls made up 14.1% of HVAC inbound calls in June 2025 and 9.8% in October 2025. Most of them arrive between 5 and 9 pm local time (Punctual Pros demand model).
- Trades lose 30-40% of off-hours calls (Voice AI research).
- Across home services, 52% of callers reach a person. The figure is 65% for calls longer than 15 seconds (Voice AI research).
- AI voice agents answer around the clock. One vendor reports they book 70% of calls, and 90% when crews have open slots. The typical human booking rate is 42%. These are vendor-reported and unaudited figures, so treat them as ranges (Voice AI research).

| Measure | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Off-hours share of HVAC calls, June | 14.1% | Punctual Pros demand model |
| Off-hours calls trades lose | 30-40% | Voice AI research |
| After-hours loss assumed in our model | 35% (est.) | Voice AI research |
| After-hours jobs recoverable with an AI agent | ~$390,000 a year (est.) | Voice AI research |

## What we cannot confirm

- **Staffing:** which hours a dispatcher or answering service covers today.
- **Answer rate at 2am:** our actual answer rate overnight. Our call volume, missed-call rate and booking rate are not public. The model infers them from estimated revenue (Voice AI research).
- **Data that would settle it:** hourly call logs from our ServiceTitan or CRM history. Answered, missed and booked counts by hour would answer both questions.

## Why timing matters now

- October is the busiest HVAC month nationally because heating systems start up (Punctual Pros demand model).
- A lead reached within 5 minutes is 21 times more likely to qualify than one reached at 30 minutes (Voice AI research).

A 2am caller with no heat will dial the next number on Google. Recovering missed calls across all hours is modelled at about $1.37M a year (est.). Overnight calls are a measurable revenue line, not a courtesy.

## Next actions

1. Pull hourly answered, missed and booked counts for the last 12 months from ServiceTitan. This confirms overnight coverage and the real after-hours loss rate.
2. Publish the actual overnight answering policy on the site once it is confirmed, so the reference answer can give a yes or no.
3. Pilot an AI voice agent for overnight and storm overflow. Measure its booking rate against current human booking before rolling it out further.
4. Re-run the recovered-revenue estimate with real call data, replacing the inferred call volume.
